approved: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2014 Measures No. 1) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would make it illegal to promote schemes that illegally release superannuation savings early.

It creates a new civil penalty in the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993, enforceable by the Commissioner of Taxation for self-managed super funds or the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority for other funds.
The explanatory memorandum notes that promoters have previously taken up to half of a member's super balance or stolen the entire amount.
Creates a new civil penalty provision in the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993.
Gives regulators the power to pursue penalties for promoting illegal early release schemes.
Targets promoters who exploit people by encouraging rollovers into fraudulent funds.
Promoters of illegal early release schemes and members of superannuation funds.

Introduced the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment Bill 2014, outlining penalties of up to $340,000 or five years' imprisonment for promoters of illegal early superannuation release schemes, transitional access to the net medical expenses tax offset until 1 July 2019 for disability aids, attendant care and aged care costs, and the addition of the National Arboretum Canberra Fund, Bali Peace Park Association and Prince's Charities Australia as deductible gift recipients.

Supported the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment Bill, noting it lists the National Arboretum Canberra Fund and Prince's Charities Australia as deductible gift recipients and phases out the net medical expenses tax offset by the 2018 to 2019 income year, and recalled that the Prime Minister said in 1995 that compulsory superannuation was one of the biggest con jobs ever foisted on the Australian people.

Said the Howard government paid off a $96 billion Beazley black hole debt by 21 April 2006, said federal Labor introduced 975 new or amending pieces of legislation and over 21,000 additional regulations in government against a coalition repeal day that will scrap more than 100 acts and 8,000 regulations, and said Labor promised 64 GP superclinics costing $650 million of which 26 remain unopened.

Criticised the removal of the low-income superannuation contribution, which will cost 20,900 people in the Blair electorate an extra $500 a year and affects 3.6 million low-income earners nationally, criticised the removal of the schoolkids bonus affecting about 19,000 children locally and 1.3 million Australians overall, and said Medicare coverage in Blair reached 88 per cent under Labor compared with 67 per cent when the current Prime Minister was health minister.

Opposed the proposed GP tax, saying more than 980,000 Medicare users in Scullin would pay $5.9 million a year, criticised delaying the superannuation guarantee increase from 9.25 to 12 per cent by 2019 which would have boosted savings for 8.4 million Australians by more than $500 billion by 2037, and said removing the low-income superannuation contribution hits 2.1 million Australian women.

Supported reinvesting the net medical expenses tax offset phase-out savings of more than $400 million into health care, criticised an average 8 per cent rise in private health insurance premiums as the biggest increase in a decade, and said a proposed $6 GP tax would cost residents of Chifley an extra $8.3 million a year.

Discussed the importance of encouraging young Australians to start superannuation savings early, and outlined the financial system inquiry whose terms of reference were released on 20 December 2013, with an interim report due in mid-2014 and a final report due to the Treasurer by November 2014.

Opposed the proposed GP tax, citing a 2009 Harvard study finding about 45,000 American deaths from delayed treatment due to cost, said the United States spends 17.7 per cent of GDP on health care compared with Australia's OECD-average level, and criticised the government for freezing the superannuation guarantee at 9¼ per cent and scrapping the low-income superannuation contribution for individuals earning $37,000 or less, retrospective from 1 July 2013.

Supported phasing out the poorly targeted net medical expenses tax offset, projected to save nearly $1 billion over four years, but urged the government to reinvest the savings in Medicare and the NDIS rather than impose a $6 GP tax that could take $4.5 million from Bendigo households, and cited the Geelong NDIS trial where one family's son received an extra $15,000 a year in support.

Introduced the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2014 Measures No. 1) Bill 2014, which adds penalties for promoters of illegal early superannuation release schemes, phases out the net medical expenses tax offset with transitional arrangements to 2019, and adds three new deductible gift recipients, while dismissing the opposition's amendment as irrelevant and criticising the member for Bendigo's comments on NDIS sustainability.
